activity_context.topic_title: The Shortest Distance Between a Plane and a Point

feedback.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-1,2,-3)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨1,-5,3⟩)\cdot ⟨1,0,4⟩=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(1,-5,3).$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-5,3⟩-⟨-1,2,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-7,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨1,0,4⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot 1+(-7)\cdot 0+6\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+0+24|}{\sqrt{1+16}} \\  & =\frac{|26|}{\sqrt{17}} \\  & =\frac{26\sqrt{17}}{17}\end{aligned}
$$
